what_this_proves: The schema check reports the alembic revision a REAL PostgreSQL is on, against the head this build carries, and says fail with both revisions named when the database is behind - the state a failed migration leaves and the state nothing used to notice.
method: app.release.schema.schema_state was run against the development PostgreSQL (real server, real alembic_version table). The row was then moved back one revision, the check re-run, and the row restored and re-read to confirm the restore.

observations.state: database moved one revision behind (the shape of a failed migration)

schema_state.head: 0040_device_build_identity
schema_state.error: database is at 0039_owner_media_playbacks, this build expects 0040_device_build_identity

build_identity.shape: 16 lowercase hex, folded from every app/**/*.py by path and sha256
build_identity.why: app_version has been 0.1.0 for every release production ever had, and version reads 'unknown' whenever the host exported no sha; neither can tell two images apart. This mirrors the device's AgentInfo.BuildId (ADR-0118).

scope_note: This proves the SERVER half against a real database. The release scripts' half (a failed migration stopping a promotion, exit 82; a schema behind its tree refused, exit 83) is PROVEN_AUTOMATED: scripts/tests/cloud-release-bluegreen.tests.ps1 and scripts/tests/cloud-release.tests.ps1 drive the real scripts under Git Bash against a fake docker that now CAN fail a migration - it could not before 2026-09-12, which is why no test ever saw the defect. Each case was proven RED against the unfixed scripts first.
not_proven_here: A blue/green promotion on the production host refusing a real failed migration. That needs a production release, which is an owner-gated promotion.
